claims.text: Models were trained using SGD with Nesterov momentum (0.9) and a weight decay of 10^-4.
claims.reason: Paper states (Section 4.2): 'we use a weight decay of 10^-4 and a Nesterov momentum of 0.9 without dampening'.

claims.text: The initial learning rate was set to 0.1 and decreased by a factor of 10 at 50% and 75% of training for CIFAR/SVHN; epochs 30 and 60 for ImageNet.
claims.reason: Paper states (Section 4.2): 'The initial learning rate is set to 0.1, and is divided by 10 at 50% and 75% of the total number of training epochs' for CIFAR/SVHN, and 'lowered by 10 times at epoch 30 and 60' for ImageNet.

claims.text: Batch sizes varied by dataset: 64 for CIFAR/SVHN and 256 for ImageNet.
claims.reason: Paper states (Section 4.2): 'On CIFAR and SVHN we train using batch size 64' and 'On ImageNet, we train models for 90 epochs with a batch size of 256'.

claims.text: For datasets without data augmentation, dropout (rate 0.2) was added after each convolutional layer to prevent overfitting.
claims.reason: Paper states (Section 4.2) dropout is added 'after each convolutional layer (except the first one)' — the summary incorrectly omits the exception for the first convolutional layer.

claims.text: CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 consist of 32x32 pixel natural images with 10 and 100 classes; training sets contain 50,000 images.
claims.reason: Paper states (Section 4.1): 'colored natural images with 32x32 pixels. CIFAR-10 (C10) consists of images drawn from 10 and CIFAR-100 (C100) from 100 classes. The training and test sets contain 50,000 and 10,000 images respectively'.

claims.text: SVHN contains 32x32 colored digit images with 73,257 training images.
claims.reason: Paper states (Section 4.1): 'The Street View House Numbers (SVHN) dataset contains 32x32 colored digit images. There are 73,257 images in the training set'.

claims.text: ImageNet (ILSVRC 2012) consists of 1.2 million training images across 1,000 classes.
claims.reason: Paper states (Section 4.1): 'The ILSVRC 2012 classification dataset consists 1.2 million images for training, and 50,000 for validation, from 1,000 classes'.

claims.text: Performance was compared against state-of-the-art architectures, specifically ResNet, Wide ResNet, and FractalNet.
claims.reason: Paper explicitly includes ResNet, Wide ResNet, and FractalNet in the comparison table (Table 2) and discusses them throughout the evaluation sections.

claims.text: Transition layers perform down-sampling using 1x1 convolutions and 2x2 average pooling.
claims.reason: Paper states (Section 3): 'The transition layers used in our experiments consist of a batch normalization layer and an 1x1 convolutional layer followed by a 2x2 average pooling layer'.

claims.text: Bottleneck layers (DenseNet-B) introduce 1x1 convolutions before 3x3 convolutions to reduce the number of input feature-maps and improve efficiency.
claims.reason: Paper states (Section 3): 'a 1x1 convolution can be introduced as bottleneck layer before each 3x3 convolution to reduce the number of input feature-maps, and thus to improve computational efficiency... we refer to our network with such a bottleneck layer as DenseNet-B'.

claims.text: Compression (DenseNet-C) uses a factor theta in transition layers to reduce the number of feature-maps.
claims.reason: Paper states (Section 3): 'we can reduce the number of feature-maps at transition layers... we let the following transition layer generate floor(theta*m) output feature-maps, where 0 < theta <= 1 is referred to as the compression factor... We refer the DenseNet with theta < 1 as DenseNet-C'.

claims.text: DenseNet connects every layer to every other layer within a dense block in a feed-forward fashion.
claims.reason: Paper states in the abstract: 'we introduce the Dense Convolutional Network (DenseNet), which connects each layer to every other layer in a feed-forward fashion'.

claims.text: DenseNet concatenates features from preceding layers, unlike ResNets which combine them through summation.
claims.reason: Paper states (Section 3): 'in contrast to ResNets, we never combine features through summation before they are passed into a layer; instead, we combine features by concatenating them'.

claims.text: The summary states the authors note that further accuracy gains may be possible through more detailed hyperparameter tuning, and that future work will explore using DenseNets as feature extractors for other computer vision tasks.
claims.reason: Paper's conclusion states: 'we believe that further gains in accuracy of DenseNets may be obtained by more detailed tuning of hyperparameters' and 'DenseNets may be good feature extractors for various computer vision tasks... We plan to study such feature transfer with DenseNets in future work'.
